title: Managed Git hook text
responsibility: Renders stage-specific hook wrappers that chain existing hooks and run Harness only in opted-in worktrees.

inputs.name: hookScript.stage
inputs.description: Stage to render, normally pre-push or commit-msg. Only commit-msg hands Harness the message file path as an argument with no stdin, and every other string takes the piped-stdin branch; the value is inserted into the script text and file names without escaping or validation.

inputs.name: managedHook.text
inputs.description: The text of an existing hook file, searched for the marker harness-managed hook at any position. The text is only searched, never parsed, so a hook that merely mentions the marker also counts as managed.

inputs.name: stageFile.stage
inputs.description: The stage whose opt-in file name is wanted: pre-push maps to the original harness-hooks file, and any other string maps to harness-hooks- followed by that string. The value is not checked against the offered stages, and the function only builds the name as a string without touching the filesystem.

outputs.name: hookMarker
outputs.description: The fixed marker text harness-managed hook, which each wrapper writes into its header comment and managedHook searches for as a plain substring.

outputs.name: chainedSuffix
outputs.description: The suffix .harness-chained, appended to the stage name to form the file beside the wrapper that keeps a hook which was already there. The wrapper runs that file first only when it exists and is executable.

outputs.name: enabledFile
outputs.description: The per-worktree opt-in file name harness-hooks, read from each worktree's own Git directory, which opts a worktree into the pre-push stage and holds its Harness command. Every version of Harness has written this name, so it means a push and nothing else.

outputs.name: hookStages
outputs.description: The stages Harness offers, in this order: pre-push, where a push is verified, and commit-msg, where the message of a commit is measured. hookScript and stageFile accept any string and do not check it against this list.

outputs.name: stageFile
outputs.description: The opt-in file name for a stage: harness-hooks for pre-push, otherwise harness-hooks- followed by the stage, so commit-msg gives harness-hooks-commit-msg. The name is built as a string only, and nothing is created or checked on disk.

outputs.name: hookScript
outputs.description: Shell script text for one stage's hook wrapper: it runs an executable chained hook first and exits with that hook's status if it fails, then exits 0 when there is no Git directory or no opt-in file, and otherwise runs the Harness command stored in the opt-in file. Producing the text does not install or run the hook.
examples:
#!/bin/sh
# harness-managed hook: pre-push. Written by "harness hooks install"; remove it with
# "harness hooks uninstall". A hook that was already here is kept beside this file and
# runs first.
hook_dir=$(dirname "$0")
input=$(cat)
newline='
'
chained="$hook_dir/pre-push.harness-chained"
if [ -x "$chained" ]; then
	printf '%s' "${input:+$input$newline}" | "$chained" "$@" || exit $?
fi
git_dir=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
[ -f "$git_dir/harness-hooks" ] || exit 0
harness=$(cat "$git_dir/harness-hooks")
printf '%s' "${input:+$input$newline}" | sh -c "$harness hooks run pre-push"
#!/bin/sh
# harness-managed hook: commit-msg. Written by "harness hooks install"; remove it with
# "harness hooks uninstall". A hook that was already here is kept beside this file and
# runs first.
hook_dir=$(dirname "$0")
chained="$hook_dir/commit-msg.harness-chained"
if [ -x "$chained" ]; then
	"$chained" "$@" || exit $?
fi
git_dir=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
[ -f "$git_dir/harness-hooks-commit-msg" ] || exit 0
harness=$(cat "$git_dir/harness-hooks-commit-msg")
sh -c "$harness hooks run commit-msg \"\$1\"" harness-hook "$1" </dev/null

outputs.name: managedHook
outputs.description: True when the text contains the managed marker anywhere, and false otherwise. It is a substring check, so a hook that only mentions the marker is reported as managed.
